title: Two-frequency forecast gains depend on flux processing in Kepler quarters 12 and 13 near KIC 8462852
abstract: We test whether two stable frequencies can explain changes in the known 0.88-day signal near KIC 8462852. We fit three harmonics per frequency to Kepler release 25 quarters 9 to 11 and freeze the periodic terms for quarters 12 and 13. With a five-day quadratic baseline, two frequencies increase later squared error by 2.23 percent in aperture flux but reduce it by 6.27 percent in corrected flux. Conditional ten-day block intervals are -7.74 to 1.46 percent and 2.14 to 10.12 percent for error reduction. Aperture-flux gains with three-day and eight-day baselines are near zero. The tests do not give stable support for the tested beating model. They do not rule out other beating models or identify a source. The products share exposures. Early-fit uncertainty, aperture changes and residual noise limit the result. No independent instrument is tested and no new planet is found. Code, aggregate fits, figures, input hashes and separate-scratch retrieval steps are included.
